name: featsel
description: In this paper, we introduce featsel, a framework for benchmarking of feature selection algorithms and cost functions. This framework allows the user to deal with the search space as a Boolean lattice and has its core coded in C++ for computational efficiency purposes. Moreover, featsel includes Perl scripts to add new algorithms and/or cost functions, generate random instances, plot graphs and organize results into tables. Besides, this framework already comes with dozens of algorithms and cost functions for benchmarking experiments. We also provide illustrative examples, in which featsel outperforms the popular Weka workbench in feature selection procedures on data sets from the UCI Machine Learning Repository.
general_score_metric: classification accuracy (of downstream models) and computational/cost metrics
reputation: A research-purpose framework cited in feature-selection literature; used by researchers needing a customizable, efficient benchmark rather than a broad community standard.
notes: Non-LLM, research-focused framework; uses many UCI-style datasets (often small), so results may not generalize to large-scale modern data; includes runtime/cost considerations and requires domain knowledge to choose appropriate cost functions.
